<reason>B convincingly separated the value of creative renewal from the justification for increasing this particular budget tier. A raised a meaningful concern about incentives favoring sequels, but never adequately established underinvestment: contraction, successful originals, and spectacular sequel failures did not resolve the marginal investment comparison. B directly answered the pressure questions, incorporated long-term value, and challenged A’s unsupported profitability claims. A repeatedly portrayed selective investment as refusing to invest, despite B explicitly allowing dollars to move toward promising originals.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>When A claimed that only mid-budget production could renew the slate at scale, B distinguished production budget from production frequency: studios could fund multiple microbudget projects. B also explained that acquisition markups can purchase information and reduce uncertainty. These replies undermined A’s attempt to dismiss alternative renewal strategies.</best_rebuttal>
